objectives.text: Keep the Beijing tie that replaced Taipei in 2004 and the aid that came with it. A joint communique was signed in Beijing on 23 March 2004; China then offered US$12 million: US$6 million of budget support for 2004 and US$1 million a year for six years. Reading from the Wikipedia index only: the aid terms are not checked against a Chinese or Dominican primary text.

constraints.text: US assistance runs through other channels. Washington's aid to Dominica is mainly routed through the World Bank, the Caribbean Development Bank and the USAID office in Bridgetown, Barbados, so Dominica has no bilateral US aid line of its own to bargain with.

paradoxes.text: Dominica signed a Bilateral Immunity Agreement with the United States (Article 98 of the Rome Statute), shielding US personnel from the International Criminal Court, while its China tie was built on the 2004 switch. Each patron's terms pull against the other's, and the state carries both.

grand_strategy.reading: Dominica is a small state whose foreign policy is a set of separate deals rather than an alignment: Beijing bought recognition in 2004 with aid, Washington and London hold the older ties through assistance channels and treaties, and the Caribbean bodies (CARICOM and the OECS) are where it speaks as one of many. Its strategic weight is low, so its moves are chosen for what they bring in, and the card can say little about the economy (citizenship by investment, the geothermal project) or the hurricane constraint until those are sourced. The gaps are the point of this first pass: the 2025 US posture and the China debt are not yet read in a source that could support them.

stances.note: Transactional. The 23 March 2004 joint communique moved recognition from Taipei to Beijing and brought US$12 million of aid (US$6 million budget support for 2004, US$1 million a year for six years), per the Wikipedia index. Partner, not ally: no treaty read. Bond none: no shared identity and no open grievance. Trend stable is our reading, not sourced; the 2025-26 debt and policing questions were not read. Confidence C: one tier 4 pointer, grade and bond are our reading.
